revisions.title: Age separates the singing choruses from myth-telling
revisions.body: The Sidonian story is marked as improbable but useful as a paradigm for legislation. The Athenian then orders participation by age: children and men up to thirty sing in distinct choruses, while men over thirty through sixty form a third singing group. Those beyond the singing age are left as myth-tellers about the same ethical matters because they can no longer bear songs. After describing older men’s reluctance to sing, he frames a legislative proposal to encourage their participation.

body: "The Sidonian story is marked as improbable but useful as a paradigm for legislation. The Athenian then separates the choruses by age: children and men up to thirty sing in the first two, while men over thirty through sixty form a third singing group later discussed as a chorus of Dionysus. Only after that singing range does he assign those who can no longer bear songs to myth-telling about the same ethical matters. Wine is then proposed for those from forty onward as a remedy for old age's harshness, making participation in song less shameful and more willing."
